definition: Poignant means piercingly moving, touching the feelings with a sharp sting of sadness.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word poignant. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know poignant should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The most poignant item in the time capsule was a wish list from 1961: every child had asked for something the town could no longer make.
Touching is milder than poignant — it warms the heart gently, while poignant pierces it.
Heartrending goes further than poignant — grief that tears at an audience, rather than a sharp, bittersweet pang.

Affecting means it stirs real emotion — an affecting speech leaves the room moved, maybe misty-eyed. Poignant is more precise about the sensation: it pierces, with a sharp and usually bittersweet sting, true to a root meaning 'to prick.' Affecting moves you; poignant leaves a small exact wound.

Bittersweet names the blend inside a feeling: pleasure and sadness in the same breath, the last day of a good summer. Poignant describes what a moment does to you — it pierces. Many poignant things are bittersweet, but bittersweet measures the mixture, and poignant measures the sting.

When my grandfather's flip phone finally died, the family gathered around a laptop to hear the one voicemail my mother had saved from it.
It was thirty seconds long and completely ordinary: he was calling to say the tomatoes had come in, and that she should stop by Saturday.
Nobody expected the message to be poignant.
It was just weather, tomatoes, Saturday.
But at the last second he said, 'Don't work too hard, kiddo' — and the word kiddo, in that voice, went through the room like a needle.
My mother laughed and cried at the same time.
The sweetness of it was exactly what made it sting; we played it twice and then sat quiet a while.
